subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which session identity and token-accounting fields may be shown in user-facing overflow errors across private and shared channels?
rationale: The implementation boundary is clear, but repository automation cannot decide whether raw session keys/channel IDs are acceptable or how observed, estimated, and stale token values should be represented as product policy.

options.title: Approve redacted structured diagnostics
options.body: Show a human-safe display label, provider/model, effective budget, and explicitly qualified token usage while excluding raw session keys, transcript paths, and request-time filesystem stats.

options.title: Keep specifics in trusted logs
options.body: Leave channel-visible copy concise and expose detailed identity and token diagnostics only through redacted debug logs or an operator inspection surface.

options.title: Defer to broader context telemetry
options.body: Keep this issue open until a unified context-status and warning design defines labels, thresholds, estimates, and post-compaction notifications together.

recommendation.title: Approve redacted structured diagnostics
recommendation.body: Show a human-safe display label, provider/model, effective budget, and explicitly qualified token usage while excluding raw session keys, transcript paths, and request-time filesystem stats.

likelyOwner.reason: They previously reviewed this exact issue and have the strongest recent history spanning runner recovery, compaction diagnostics, and user-facing auto-reply behavior.
